title: Image and font optimization
description: Learn about Image and font optimization. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Images and fonts are often the largest resources on a web page. Optimizing them can dramatically improve load times, reduce bandwidth usage, and enhance user experience. Modern web technologies provide many tools and techniques for efficient image and font delivery.
Image Optimization Strategies

Image optimization involves choosing the right format, compressing effectively, serving appropriate sizes, and implementing modern loading techniques. A well-optimized image strategy can reduce image sizes by 50-80% while maintaining visual quality.
Modern Image Formats

Next-generation image formats offer superior compression compared to traditional formats like JPEG and PNG. WebP typically provides 25-35% better compression than JPEG, while AVIF can achieve 50% better compression.

data.title: Responsive Images with Multiple Formats
data.content: Serve modern formats with fallbacks using picture element.

data.text: Responsive Images
Serve appropriately sized images based on the user's device and viewport. This prevents mobile users from downloading desktop-sized images they don't need.

data.title: Responsive Image with srcset
data.content: Serve different image sizes for different viewports.

data.text: Image Compression
Use lossy compression for photographs and lossless compression for graphics. Tools like ImageOptim, TinyPNG, or sharp (Node.js) can automatically optimize images during build time.

data.title: Automatic Image Optimization with Next.js
data.content: Use Next.js Image component for automatic optimization.

data.text: Font Optimization
Fonts can block rendering and cause layout shifts. Optimize fonts by using modern formats, subsetting, and implementing proper loading strategies to ensure fast, stable text rendering.
Modern Font Formats
WOFF2 is the modern standard for web fonts, offering 30% better compression than WOFF. Use WOFF2 with WOFF fallback for broader browser support.

data.title: Font Format Fallback Strategy
data.content: Serve modern font formats with appropriate fallbacks.

data.text: Font Subsetting
Subset fonts to include only the characters you actually use. This can reduce font file sizes by 60-90%. Most font files include thousands of characters you'll never need.

data.title: Font Subsetting with glyphhanger
data.content: Subset fonts to include only used characters.
data.code:
# Install glyphhanger
npm install -g glyphhanger

# Subset font to only used characters
glyphhanger --subset=*.html --formats=woff2,woff --whitespace=woff2

# Or specify specific characters
glyphhanger --whitespace=woff2 --LATIN --GREEK --digits

data.text: Font Loading Strategies
Use font-display: swap to show text immediately with a fallback font, preventing invisible text (FOIT). For critical fonts, consider preloading to ensure they're available quickly.

data.title: Font Loading Best Practices
data.code:
<!-- Preload critical fonts -->
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/critical.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>

<!-- Font with swap strategy -->
<style>
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Main Font';
  src: url('/fonts/main.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-display: swap; /* Show fallback immediately */
}

body {
  font-family: 'Main Font', system-ui, sans-serif;
}
</style>

data.text: Preventing Layout Shift from Fonts
Font loading can cause Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) when the web font loads and changes text rendering. Reserve space for text and use font-display: swap to minimize this impact.

data.title: Reserve Space for Text
data.content: Prevent layout shift by reserving text space.

data.title: Font Fallback Chain
data.text: Always provide a robust font fallback chain ending with system fonts. This ensures text is always readable, even if custom fonts fail to load.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use modern image formats (WebP, AVIF) with fallbacks for older browsers
Implement responsive images with srcset and sizes attributes
Compress images appropriately (lossy for photos, lossless for graphics)
Use WOFF2 font format with WOFF fallback
Subset fonts to include only characters you actually use
Implement font-display: swap to prevent invisible text
Preload critical fonts and reserve space to prevent layout shift
Automate optimization in your build process
data.takeaway: Image and font optimization are high-impact, low-effort optimizations that significantly improve page load performance and user experience.
